name: energyflowx
description: Engineering calculations for fluids, air and pipework: validated thermophysical properties for 29 fluids from reference equations of state, HVAC process chains, pipe and duct sizing against real product catalogues, and full hydraulic network solving for liquids, gases and steam, with pumps, compressors with heat recovery, heat exchangers, storage tanks and receivers, in steady state or over time. Connects the EnergyFlowX members MCP server, every tool behind one sign-in, and adds the method for using them well.

interface.shortDescription: Fluid properties, HVAC processes, pipe sizing and hydraulic networks
interface.longDescription: Engineering calculations for fluids, air and pipework from the EnergyFlowX engines. Validated thermophysical properties for 29 fluids from reference equations of state, with the method and validity range on every result. Air-handling processes: heating, cooling with condensate, mixing, heat recovery, fans and humidification. Pipe and duct sizing against real product catalogues. Hydraulic network design and solving for liquids, gases and steam, with pumps, compressors, heat exchangers, tanks and receivers, steady or over time, handed over as a study page, a CAD drawing (DXF) and a PDF. Four skills teach the method: which inputs matter, what to check before quoting a number, and how to present a result.
defaultPrompt: What are the density and viscosity of 30% propylene glycol at 5 °C?
Which pipe size for 2 kg/s of water at 70 °C, at most 1.5 m/s?
Heat 5000 m3/h of outdoor air from -10 °C, 80% RH to 20 °C. What heating power?

positive.description: A thermophysical property lookup for liquid water, computed from the IAPWS-IF97 reference formulation rather than remembered.
positive.prompt: What are the density, specific heat and dynamic viscosity of water at 60 °C and 3 bar?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_fluid_properties for LIQUID_WATER at 60 °C and 3 bar and reports the density as about 983 kg/m3, the specific heat as about 4.18 kJ/(kg·K) and the dynamic viscosity as about 0.47 mPa·s, naming IAPWS-IF97 as the method the tool returned.

positive.description: A refrigerant saturation lookup. R134a is a members-only fluid, so this also shows that the signed-in test account reaches the members tools.
positive.prompt: At what temperature does R134a boil at 3 bar absolute, and what is its latent heat there?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_saturation_properties for R134A at 3 bar and reports a saturation temperature of about 0.7 °C, with the latent heat of vaporisation and the saturated liquid and vapour densities the tool returns.

positive.description: An air-handling process: heating cold outdoor air in a heating coil, with the psychrometric state before and after.
positive.prompt: Heat 5000 m3/h of outdoor air from -10 °C and 80% relative humidity to 20 °C. What heating power does the coil need, and what is the relative humidity after it?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls calculate_air_process with one HEATING step, an inlet of 5000 m3/h at -10 °C and 80% and a target of 20 °C. Reports the coil duty the tool returns, of the order of 50 to 60 kW, and the outlet relative humidity of about 9%, since heating adds no moisture.

positive.description: Pipe sizing against a real product catalogue: the smallest catalogue size that meets a velocity limit, with the size below and the limit it breaks.
positive.prompt: Which size of steel pipe do I need for 2 kg/s of water at 70 °C if the velocity must stay at or below 1.5 m/s? Show the size below too.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds a steel pipe product with search_conduit_catalog, then calls select_conduit_size with 2 kg/s of water at 70 °C and a maximum velocity of 1.5 m/s. Reports the selected nominal size with its inner diameter, velocity and pressure drop per metre, and the next size down with the velocity by which it exceeds 1.5 m/s.

positive.description: A hydraulic network built, checked, solved and reported: a small closed heating loop with a pump and two radiators, handed over as a study page, a CAD drawing (DXF) and a PDF.
positive.prompt: Design a small closed heating loop with EnergyFlowX: a circulation pump, about 20 m of DN25 supply and return pipe, and two radiators of 3 kW each at 70/50 °C. Solve it and give me the report.
positive.expected_behavior: Asks for or states any missing input it assumes (such as the pump duty or the fill pressure), opens a session, builds the loop with hydronic_edit, checks the drawing with hydronic_preview, solves it, and calls hydronic_report. Shows the verdict and the network image, and gives the links to the study page, the DXF drawing and the PDF. Each radiator carries about 0.036 kg/s of water (3 kW over a 20 K drop).

negative.description: A general question with no engineering calculation in it. EnergyFlowX should not be called.
negative.prompt: What will the weather be like in Warsaw tomorrow?

negative.description: An electrical design question. EnergyFlowX covers fluids, air and pipework, not electrical circuits, so it should not be called and should not be presented as able to answer it.
negative.prompt: What cross-section of copper cable do I need for a 32 A circuit 40 m long?

negative.description: A pressure-surge (water hammer) analysis. EnergyFlowX solves networks steady or over time but does not model pressure waves, so it should not be used to produce a surge pressure.
negative.prompt: Calculate the peak pressure surge when a quick-closing valve shuts at the end of a 300 m DN150 water main.

publication.release_notes: First release in the OpenAI plugin directory: validated fluid properties for 29 fluids, air-handling processes, pipe and duct sizing against real product catalogues, and hydraulic network design and solving with a study page, a DXF drawing and a PDF. Four skills teach the method. Sign in with a free EnergyFlowX account.
